reader_summary: I understand this as a lesson about deciding which trained candidate to deliver. Completing the requested updates and changing the intended parameters proves that training ran, but it does not prove useful answers on new questions. Validation chooses among the unchanged base and corrections saved after 1,039 and 2,077 updates. The final test is reserved until weights, data and generation settings are fixed. A correction is accepted only when all answers end normally, each use meets its retention threshold and the pre-agreed combined score is strictly better than the base. The 1,039-update correction improves the shown photo results from 16/28 to 23/28 and 31/56 to 53/56, while correct-transcript chat drops from 4/4 to 2/4 and real-ASR chat drops from 3/4 to 2/4. The perfect-text route bypasses recognition errors, so its regression shows that the answer component itself can be responsible. The longer candidate also fails the chat threshold, and each correction has three answers reaching the 384-new-token limit without normal termination. The text therefore retains the base with the same recognizer, while explicitly acknowledging that the base also makes mistakes and unfinished answers. These are prose-cited earlier experiment results, not experiments I reproduced. A lower demonstration prediction cost and normal termination each give limited evidence; neither substitutes for checking complete answer content.

terminology.details: Validation chooses settings; the final test is held out until the choice is fixed. The base is the unchanged original model, the candidate is a saved correction, and the acceptance conditions are a conjunction. Through 20.6, LoRA means a smaller trainable matrix branch added to the fixed original map; ASR is the speech recognizer producing a transcript. Gradients guide parameter updates and an optimizer performs them in the toy example. Termination is explicitly separated from answer correctness. Token is only inferable as an encoded generation unit here, a nonblocking terminology note, because the exact encoding is unnecessary for the decision exercise.

examples.details: The study-method/mock-exam analogy makes the validation/final-test timing understandable. The table has distinct denominators: 28 short photo descriptions, 56 visible-fact questions, and four questions in each chat route. I can compare the same route before and after correction, rather than merge these into one universal rate. The small denominators and repeated questions per picture are explicitly cautioned against broad inference. 1,039 and 2,077 identify saved update counts, and 384 is the maximum newly generated encoded units in the cited incomplete answers. The table is evidence of a tradeoff, not an assurance that the longer run wins.

program_explanation.details: 20.8 contains no fenced code or formula, so it has no target program to trace. I read and ran short explicitly linked prerequisite programs instead: 5.10 takes two stored validation records and replaces selected only when a later score is greater; 20.7 calls render_chat on Q/A, uses y != -100 to retain directly scored targets and locates the first one; 20.6 takes a four-value all-ones input through a fixed base plus trainable A/B branch, computes square-mean cost, backpropagates and performs one SGD update. The originals and stated small variants ran on the existing CPU virtualenv. These tiny runs do not reproduce the complete LoRA training or reported validation results.

exercise.details: I can answer both prompts directly. Correct-transcript chat removes recognition errors from the input route, so its drop from 4/4 to 2/4 cannot all be assigned to ASR. Actual-ASR chat then tests the combined recognition-and-answer route, dropping from 3/4 to 2/4. Photo improvements alone cannot satisfy the chat routes’ separate no-regression requirements, and acceptance also demands normal completion plus a strictly better agreed composite score. The section states why both corrections fail, retains the base as a fallback under the rule, and avoids calling that base broadly reliable. My exercise prediction is saved before code runs.
